newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.

text.p: Analysis of key elements in Wednesday's European Champions' League matches:
Group A
Ajax Amsterdam (Netherlands) v Glasgow Rangers (Scotland)

Rangers, bottom of the group after two defeats, have severe injury problems, particularly in attack. Scotland strikers Ally McCoist and Gordon Durie are definitely out. Dane Erik Bo Andersen has a hamstring injury and is almost certainly out. Dutchman Peter van Vossen needed stitches in an ankle injury in Saturday's 2-1 defeat at Hibernian and is doubtful for the game against his old club. Also missing are defenders Stephen Wright, Alan McLaren and David Robertson and midfielder Trevor Steven.

Ajax are similarly dogged by injury. Captain Danny Blind and Peter Hoekstra will be out for months and Richard Witschge is only now recovering. Up front, Patrick Kluivert and Finn Jari Litmanen, the club's most prolific scorer in European competition, are reported to have resumed light training. Litmanen is the likelier to play but Kluivert could be a surprise late substitute if goals are needed.
Auxerre (France) v Grasshopper Zurich (Switzerland)

Auxerre captain Sabri Lamouchi twisted an ankle in last Wednesday's friendly between France and Turkey. The midfielder still feels some pain but is confident he will play -- probably the only change in the side which struggled to beat Lens on Saturday with a late penalty. Either Antoine Sibierski, the penalty scorer, or Philippe Voileau will step down. Australian defender Ned Zelic is still out injured. Thomas Deniaud, who scored twice against Rangers in Glasgow as stand-in for injured striker Lilian Laslandes, retains his place.

Grasshopper Zurich, top of the group after wins over Rangers and Ajax, will definitely be without forward Joel Magnin who needed stitches in his forehead following injury in a 4-2 win over FC Zurich on Sunday. International midfielder Murat Yakin bruised a thigh in a match against Aarau last Wednesday but is expected to play. Defender Harald Gaemperle has Achilles tendon problems and is doubtful.
Group B
Steaua Bucharest (Romania) v Widzew Lodz (Poland)

Steaua's attacking midfielder Adrian Ilie completes three-match suspension after being sent off in the preliminary round against Belgium's Brugge. Steaua have not managed a goal or a point in their first two Champions' League games. Central defender Daniel Prodan has served a one-match ban but is doubtful because of injury.

Widzew Lodz, like Steaua without a point in the Champions' League, are expected to be without five players through injury and suspension. Ryszard Czerwiec has his foot in a cast and fellow midfielders Andrzej Michalczuk and Zbigniew Wyciszkiewicz are suspended for a match each for two bookings in the European Cup campaign. Piotr Szarpak, another midfielder, is still nursing an injury suffered in last month's defeat by Atletico Madrid. Striker Rafal Siadaczka is also likely to miss the game.
Atletico Madrid (Spain) v Borussia Dortmund (Germany)

Atletico will be without playmaker Jose Luis Caminero, who is both suspended and injured, but hope to welcome back international striker Kiko Narvaez, who missed Saturday's 2-2 home draw with Real Betis. Serbian set-piece specialist Milinko Pantic, midfielder Diego Simeone and fellow Argentine Leonardo Biagini all have minor injuries but are expected to play. Also injured is coach Radomir Antic, who strained his left ankle during practice on Sunday.

Dortmund sweeper Matthias Sammer and striker Karlheinz Riedle, both overcoming injuries, have started running again but will not be fit enough to play. Brazilian defender Julio Cesar has a slight muscle injury but can probably play.
Group C
Rapid Vienna (Austria) v Juventus (Italy)

Rapid Vienna, who suffered their first Austrian league defeat of the season when beaten 3-0 at Linz on Saturday, have no major injury worries. Bulgarian international Trifon Ivanov and Didi Kuehbauer return after missing the Linz defeat through suspension and should strengthen midfield.

Juventus, the only team with a 100 percent record in the group, also suffered their first domestic league defeat at the weekend when they lost 2-1 at Vicenza. Croatian striker Alen Boksic returns but Juventus will still be without goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi, midfielder Antonio Conte and striker Alessandro Del Piero, all injured. Michelangelo Rampulla replaces Peruzzi in goal, while Michele Padovano will probably join Christian Vieri and Boksic in attack. Serb Vladimir Jugovic and Angelo Di Livio link up with Frenchman Didier Deschamps in midfield.
Fenerbahce (Turkey) v Manchester United (England)

Fenerbahce midfielders Bulent Uygun and Tayfun Korkut are both doubtful because of injury. Uygun looked slow in Sunday's 1-0 league win over Bursaspor and was the focus of hostility from Fenerbahce fans who whistled their disapproval of the team.

Manchester United defender Gary Pallister is doubtful but manager Alex Ferguson hopes the player will recover from a back injury which recurred when he played for England last week. England defender Phil Neville has recovered from an ankle ligament injury and could be on the substitutes' bench. Forwards Paul Scholes and Jordi Cruyff are injury doubts.
Group D
Gothenburg (Sweden) v AC Milan (Italy)

Gothenburg, who secured their fourth successive Swedish league title on Saturday with a 6-0 win over Trelleborg, have no players injured or suspended. Striker Andreas Andersson scored twice against Trelleborg and is top scorer in the domestic league with 17 goals and two matches to come.

AC Milan's Marco Simone, who missed Saturday's 3-0 defeat by Roma because of an upset stomach, returns to partner Liberian George Weah in attack. Croatia's Zvonimir Boban, absent from the Roma game through suspension, reappears in midfield. Simone's return means Roberto Baggio will probably once again be relegated to the substitutes' bench. Montenegrin Dejan Savicevic is ruled out by injury. Captain Franco Baresi, who played his first competitive game in more than a month against Roma, is also a doubtful starter because of tendinitis.
Rosenborg (Norway) v Porto (Portugal)

Rosenborg hope international midfielder Karl Petter Loeken and defender Stale Stensaas will be fit to play after missing last Sunday's 4-3 defeat by Kongsvinger in the Norwegian league. Loeken has a bruised thigh while Stensaas had influenza.

Porto, top of the group after beating Milan and Gothenburg, hope Brazilian striker Artur Oliveira will have recovered from injury in Saturday's 1-0 win over Sporting in the Portuguese league. Artur needed six stitches in his right foot. Defender Rui Jorge is Porto's other fitness doubt. He also suffered a foot injury in Saturday's clash.
